decisive_items: Bilateral rales and crackles on pulmonary auscultation
Extensive macular alveolar infiltrations throughout both lungs
response.rationale: The clinical picture of high-altitude exposure, respiratory distress, cyanosis, hemoptysis, bilateral crackles, hypoxemia, and diffuse alveolar infiltrates on CT without cardiac dysfunction strongly supports high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE). Hypothermia (R2) is contradicted by normal vital signs, and reperfusion injury (R1) lacks supporting evidence.

rejected.why: Normal heart rate and blood pressure contradict hypothermia; no hypothermic symptoms or temperature findings.
No evidence of ischemia-reperfusion; rapid excavation and hemoglobin drop are nonspecific and not characteristic of reperfusion injury.
